guide.title: Reading the labs as connected series

reading_order_meaning: A curated reading order, not a claim about project chronology or code ancestry.
publication_dependency: Publish the reader guide and three linked history pieces together, no later than the implementation articles that link to the guide. These remain unscheduled drafts. Existing live and scheduled article bodies are unchanged.

articles.title: A palette generator should keep the colour you gave it
articles.description: Inside Tailwind Colour Creator: anchoring the 500 step, shaping an OKLCH scale, fitting it into sRGB and exporting the right contract for Tailwind v3 and v4.

articles.title: Celestial Globe: drawing the sky from the inside
articles.description: How a Canvas sky map combines D3 projections, stellar magnitude, layered drawing and planetary positions, and where its visual model needs careful boundaries.

articles.title: Day Lite: where the Sun meets the clock
articles.description: Building a daylight globe with Mapbox and Astronomy Engine, and separating sunrise calculations from the much messier business of local time.

articles.title: From a palette generator to Gamut, and back again
articles.description: The path from a small HSL palette tool to a broader colour system, and the OKLCH maths that travelled back. The commits reveal a useful feedback loop with different promises at each end.

articles.title: From charts to explorable models: what changed in Labs
articles.description: How Labs grew from a colour-space family tree into a collection of explorable models, and the specific changes that made the explanations easier to inspect, compare and trust.

articles.title: Kinetic: designing motion you can interrupt
articles.description: What 25 interactive animation studies reveal about springs, gestures, identity, interruption and the work needed to turn a polished effect into a usable component.

articles.title: Liquidity: two ways to make type feel fluid
articles.description: Comparing an SVG wave with 2,500 Rapier particles, including the difference between a visual mask, a collision shape and an actual fluid model.

articles.title: Making balloons feel light with Matter.js
articles.description: How Balloon Bonanza uses two bodies, three constraints and carefully chosen motion to turn a pile of circles into a tactile physics playground.

articles.title: Moth: from a drawing gallery to an observatory
articles.description: How the public view of Moth grew from a chronological drawing gallery into four views of one record, and what that change can honestly tell us.

articles.title: One photograph, fifteen ways to draw with data
articles.description: How my creative coding studies turn one image into particles, edges, sorted columns and growing regions, with the small algorithms that give each experiment its character.

articles.title: Reading the labs as connected series
articles.description: Nine routes through the experiments, connecting the original questions, the tools they became and the decisions that changed along the way.

articles.title: Rebuilding Beyond Light: making room for the reveal
articles.description: The Three.js implementation behind Beyond Light: a room made from planes, text revealed in a shader, and separate clocks for reading and bloom.

articles.title: Refract: from a sentence to a running shader
articles.description: How Refract turns a visual description into GLSL, checks the result before replacing the canvas, and separates a successful generation from a successful picture.

articles.title: Spectra: turning sound into a shader without animating every pixel in JavaScript
articles.description: The audio graph, frequency bands, smoothing and domain-warped noise behind Spectra, with a closer look at where visual response and audio measurement differ.

articles.title: Teaching a computer to paint: what the baseline taught me
articles.description: A reproducible painting experiment, from random shapes to pigment mixing and six AI art directors, and why a fixed brush schedule still mattered.

articles.title: Why this take won: making a selection score readable
articles.description: Inside Post Ready's phrase scoring: word coverage, fillers, pace and gaze, with worked examples and an interactive way to inspect the trade-offs.
